info.title: zig-waf control plane
info.description:
The versioned control-plane API. The path prefix carries the version: a breaking change to any operation takes a new prefix rather than mutating one clients already call.

Authorization is a property of the operation, not of its handler — every operation declares the action it requires, and an identity that cannot perform that action is refused before the handler runs. src/api.zig holds the same table, and a test fails the build if this document and that table disagree, because a published contract clients are written against must not describe an API that does not exist.

Error.description: The single shape every failure takes. One shape rather than per-operation bodies is deliberate: a client writes one error path, and an operation cannot invent a failure representation its callers have never seen.

code.description: A stable, machine-readable identifier for the failure. Clients branch on this; the message is for people and may be reworded.

message.description: A human-readable explanation, safe to display.

detail.description: Optional context about what specifically was wrong. Never contains credentials, tokens, or the contents of a rejected secret.

Identity.description: Who the caller is and what they may do.

email.description: The identity the credential resolves to.

role.description: The role whose permissions apply to this caller.

SessionRequest.description: Credentials presented to start a session.

password.description: The account password. Never logged, never echoed back.

expires_at.description: When the session stops being accepted.

TokenRequest.description: A request to mint an API token.

name.description: A name unique among the caller's tokens, used to revoke it.

role.description: The role the token carries. It cannot exceed the issuer's own role.

expires_in_seconds.description: Lifetime from issuance. A token without an expiry is a credential nobody remembers to revoke, so this is required.

Token.description: A freshly issued token. The secret appears in this response and nowhere else: the control plane stores only a hash, so a lost token is reissued rather than recovered.

name.description: The token name, used to revoke it.

secret.description: The bearer credential. Returned once, at issuance.

expires_at.description: When the token stops being accepted.

node_id.description: The node identifier, assigned at enrollment and stable for its life.

hostname.description: The host the node reported at its last enrollment.

version.description: The engine version the node reported.

status.description: Lifecycle state. A node is active from enrollment until it is retired.

last_seen_at.description: The last heartbeat, or null if the node has never sent one.

NodeList.description: Enrolled nodes, with the inventory counts behind them.

EnrollmentRequest.description: An enrollment. Idempotent: re-enrolling an existing node refreshes its hostname and version rather than failing, so a node that restarts mid-enrollment is not stuck.

hostname.description: The host the node runs on.

version.description: The engine version the node runs.

last_seen_at.description: The heartbeat the control plane recorded.

LabelRequest.description: A label value used to target rollouts.

value.description: The value to set for this label key.

PolicyPublication.description: A new policy version. Versions are immutable: republishing an existing (name, version) is a conflict rather than an overwrite, because a node that already applied that version would otherwise be running different rules from one that fetches it later.

version.description: The version number, which must not already exist.

signature.description: Optional Ed25519 signature over the content, base64. A node verifies it before applying the bundle, so a bundle altered in transit is refused rather than enforced.

PolicyVersion.description: One immutable version of a policy.

signature.description: The Ed25519 signature over the content, base64, or null if the version was published unsigned.

Rule.description: One rule within a policy version.

id.description: The rule id from its `id:` action.

phase.description: The phase the rule evaluates in.

message.description: The rule's `msg:` text, empty when it declares none.

RuleList.description: The rules a policy version contains.

rules.description: The rules, in the order the engine evaluates them.

SignatureVerification.description: Whether a published version's signature verifies against the control plane's key.

verified.description: True only if a signature is present and valid. An unsigned version verifies as false rather than as trusted.

reason.description: Why verification failed, when it did.

Exclusion.description: A rule exclusion scoped to a policy.

rule_id.description: The rule the exclusion applies to.

target.description: The variable or argument excluded, e.g. `ARGS:token`.

reason.description: Why the exclusion exists. Recorded because an exclusion nobody can justify later is one nobody dares remove.

ExclusionRequest.description: An exclusion to add to a policy.

target.description: The variable or argument to exclude.

reason.description: Why this exclusion is being made.

exclusions.description: The exclusions, ordered by rule id.

RolloutState.description: Where a staged rollout stands. The counts are what `advance` is decided on: a version widens only when every node assigned it is responsive and confirmed.

version.description: The version currently assigned to the cohort.

unresponsive.description: Assigned nodes whose last heartbeat is older than the heartbeat window, or that have never sent one.

unconfirmed.description: Assigned nodes that have not reported running this version.

healthy.description: Whether the cohort is evidence the version is safe to widen: non-empty, fully responsive, and fully confirmed.

RolloutAssignment.description: The version to assign, and to whom.

node_ids.description: The nodes to assign it to.

Drift.description: A node running something other than what it was assigned.

running_version.description: The version it last reported running, or null if it has never reported one.

DriftList.description: Nodes that have drifted from their assignment.

Event.description: One security event recorded by a node.

id.description: The event's row identifier, as a string because it exceeds the range a JSON number is guaranteed to carry exactly.

action.description: What the engine did, e.g. `deny` or `pass`.

EventPage.description: A page of events. Paging is by cursor rather than offset: a page is defined by where the previous one ended, so events arriving between requests neither shift rows into a page already read nor skip rows the reader never saw.

next_occurred_at.description: Pass as `after_occurred_at` for the next page. Null when the page is the last one.

next_id.description: Pass as `after_id` for the next page, together with `next_occurred_at`. Null when the page is the last one.

EventSubmission.description: One event a node is submitting.

key.description: An idempotency key unique to this event on this node, e.g. its transaction id. Re-submitting the same key at the same `occurred_at` is skipped rather than duplicated, so a node may safely re-send a batch it never saw acknowledged. Omit it and the event is always inserted.

EventBatch.description: A batch of events to ingest, committed all-or-nothing.

events.description: The events. One commit covers the whole batch.

IngestionResult.description: What ingestion did with a batch. `received` minus `inserted` is how many were recognized as already ingested — the expected outcome of a re-sent batch, not an error.

SavedSearch.description: A named event search belonging to the caller.

name.description: The search name, unique per user.

SavedSearchRequest.description: A search to save under this name, replacing any existing one.

Alert.description: An alert rule and its delivery target.

event_action.description: The event action that fires this rule.

webhook_url.description: Where a firing alert is delivered.

signed.description: Whether deliveries carry an HMAC-SHA256 signature. The secret itself is never returned.

silenced_until.description: When the rule resumes firing, or null if it is not silenced.

name.description: A name unique among alert rules.

event_action.description: The event action that should fire it.

secret.description: Optional signing secret. When set, each delivery carries an HMAC-SHA256 signature over its body so the receiver can tell a real alert from anything else that finds the URL.

SilenceRequest.description: How long to stop a rule from firing.

until.description: When the rule resumes firing. A silence always ends: one without an expiry is an alert quietly deleted.

FailingChannel.description: A delivery target that is failing.

consecutive_failures.description: Deliveries that have failed in a row.

FailingChannelList.description: Alert channels whose deliveries are failing — the alerts an operator is not receiving, which is the failure mode an alerting system cannot report through itself.

SettingRequest.description: A value to store under this key.

Health.description: Whether the control plane can serve. Reports the schema version because a process that connects to a database it cannot use is not healthy, however willing it is to answer.

detail.description: What is degraded, when something is.

EnrollmentTokenRequest.description: A one-time enrollment token to issue.

label.description: What the token was issued for, e.g. a rack or an autoscaling group. Also how it is withdrawn.

ttl_seconds.description: How long the token may be claimed for. Required: a token without an expiry is a credential nobody remembers to revoke.

EnrollmentToken.description: A freshly issued enrollment token. The secret is returned here and nowhere else — only its hash is stored — so a token that is lost is reissued rather than recovered.

secret.description: The value a node presents once to enroll.

expires_at.description: After this, the token cannot be claimed.

Certificate.description: A certificate a node authenticates with. The row outlives the certificate deliberately: "what was this node using in March" is the question an incident actually asks.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the DER encoding, lowercase hex — what an mTLS terminator computes from the presented certificate.

issued_at.description: When the control plane recorded it.

revoked_at.description: When it was revoked, or null if it has not been.

revocation_reason.description: Why it was revoked, or null. Always present when revoked_at is: an unexplained revocation reads as a mistake, and the safe reading of a mistake is to re-issue.

CertificateList.description: The certificates recorded for a node, newest expiry first. More than one is active during a rotation, which overlaps on purpose.

active.description: How many are unrevoked and unexpired.

CertificateRotation.description: Record a newly issued certificate for a node. The outgoing certificate is left valid until it expires: a rotation that cut over instantly would take away the identity of a request already in flight.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the new certificate's DER encoding, lowercase hex. Rejected in any other form, since a fingerprint that does not match what a terminator computes can never authenticate anything.

lifetime_seconds.description: How long the new certificate is valid. Short is the point: a stolen key that expires tomorrow has to be stolen again.

CapabilityReport.description: What a node can do and what protocol version it speaks.

capabilities.description: The features the node supports, by name. Anything absent is treated as unsupported, because sending a node rules it cannot evaluate makes it enforce less than the operator believes without failing.

NegotiatedProtocol.description: The version both sides will speak — the older of the two, so a fleet can be upgraded one node at a time. A node below the supported minimum is refused rather than served on a best-effort basis.

RotationDueList.description: Nodes with no certificate that will still be valid at the horizon — the work list a rotation job walks.

within_seconds.description: The horizon the list was computed for.

Forbidden.description: The identity may not perform this operation
